title: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_code: KS4 Chemistry: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
standard_text: A simple model of the atom: protons, neutrons and electrons; the size and mass of atoms; atomic number, mass number and isotopes; relative atomic mass; the development of the model of the atom; electronic structure; the periodic table, its development (Mendeleev) and groups 0, 1 and 7; metals and non-metals.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on atomic structure: protons, neutrons and electrons, isotopes, relative atomic mass, electron shells, the history of the atom and the periodic table. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons; electrons fill shells 2, 8, 8.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons in shells.

  • Atomic number = protons. Mass number = protons + neutrons. Neutrons = mass number − atomic number.
  • Isotopes have different numbers of neutrons. Electrons fill shells 2, 8, 8.
  • Groups share the same number of outer electrons, so they react in similar ways.
Example

Sodium: atomic number 11, mass number 23. Neutrons?

23 − 11

Answer: 12

Example

Electron structure of chlorine (17)?

2 + 8 + 7

Answer: 2, 8, 7

Common mistakes

  • Thinking mass number is the number of protons.
  • Thinking isotopes have different numbers of protons.
  • Thinking reactivity increases down group 7.

faq.q: How do you work out the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons?
faq.a: Protons = atomic number. In a neutral atom electrons = protons. Neutrons = mass number − atomic number.
Atoms of the same element (same number of protons) with different numbers of neutrons, so they have different mass numbers.

faq.q: How has the model of the atom changed?
faq.a: Dalton's solid spheres, Thomson's plum pudding, Rutherford's nuclear model, Bohr's shells and Chadwick's neutron each followed new evidence.

items.q: A neutral atom of copper has a mass number of 63. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 29.

items.q: A neutral atom of sodium has a mass number of 23. How many electrons does it have?
items.e: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons = 11.

items.q: How many protons are in an atom of sodium-23?
items.e: The atomic number (11) is the number of protons.

items.q: An atom has 33 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: The number of protons decides the element.

items.q: An atom has 42 neutrons and 33 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: Use the protons (33), not the neutrons.

items.q: An atom has 38 protons and 49 neutrons. What is its mass number?
How many neutrons are in an atom of silver-107?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 107 − 47 = 60.

items.q: How many neutrons are in <sup>80</sup><sub>34</sub>Se?
Roughly how big is an atom?
items.e: The nucleus is about 1/10,000 of that.

items.q: Where is most of the mass of an atom?
items.e: Protons and neutrons.

items.q: What is an isotope?
c: an atom of the same element with a different number of neutrons
an atom with a different number of protons
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass number.

items.q: An atom has 2 protons. Which element is it?
items.e: The number of protons decides the element.

items.q: How many neutrons are in <sup>11</sup><sub>5</sub>B?
How many protons are in an atom of fluorine-21?
items.e: The atomic number (9) is the number of protons.

items.q: What are the relative charges of a proton, a neutron and an electron?
items.e: Atoms are neutral overall.

items.q: An atom has 13 protons and 15 neutrons. What is its mass number?
How many neutrons are in an atom of lead-210?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 210 − 82 = 128.

items.q: How many neutrons are in an atom of carbon-14?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 14 − 6 = 8.

items.q: Why does an atom have no overall charge?
c: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
items.e: Balanced charges.

items.q: An atom has 33 protons and 43 neutrons. What is its mass number?
How many more neutrons does <sup>10</sup>Be have than <sup>9</sup>Be?
How does a phosphorus atom form the ion P<sup>3−</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: Leo finds that element X has two isotopes: 15% has mass 12 u and 85% has mass 14 u. What is the relative atomic mass?
Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass numbers.

items.q: How many more neutrons does <sup>65</sup>Cu have than <sup>63</sup>Cu?
How does a chlorine atom form the ion Cl<sup>−</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass numbers.

Phosphorus-31 and phosphorus-33 are isotopes. What do they have the same number of?

items.q: Alfie finds that element X has two isotopes: 25% has mass 23 u and 75% has mass 25 u. What is the relative atomic mass?
How does a rubidium atom form the ion Rb<sup>+</sup>?
items.e: Ions form by gaining or losing electrons.

items.q: How many electrons are in the ion Cl<sup>−</sup>?
items.e: 17 protons; charge −1 means 18 electrons.

items.q: Lead-208 and lead-209 are isotopes. What do they have the same number of?
items.e: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.

items.q: Aisha finds that element X has two isotopes: 15% has mass 46 u and 85% has mass 48 u. What is the relative atomic mass?
Jack finds that element X has two isotopes: 30% has mass 75 u and 70% has mass 77 u. What is the relative atomic mass?
How many electrons are in the ion S<sup>2−</sup>?
items.e: 16 protons; charge −2 means 18 electrons.

items.q: How many protons are in the ion Rb<sup>+</sup>?
items.e: Forming an ion changes electrons, not protons.

items.q: What is the electron arrangement (shells) of an argon atom (18 electrons)?
items.e: Fill 2, then 8, then 8, then 2.

items.q: What did Dmitri Mendeleev contribute?
c: He suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at fixed distances (shells).
He showed with the alpha scattering experiment that the atom has a small, dense, positive nucleus.
He arranged the elements by atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements.
items.e: Models change with evidence.

items.e: Valence electrons are in the outer shell.

items.q: A neon atom has the electron arrangement 2, 8. How many valence electrons does it have?
